newsitem.title: UK: Brady bond trade continues capped ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Brady bond trade continues capped ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices hovered around overnight levels on Tuesday ahead of the Federal Reserve's key policy meeting, Brady bond traders said.
"Everyone has shut up shop and is sitting on their hands," an emerging market analyst said.
"If the Fed hikes rates it won't be a surprise and emerging market debt spreads will widen in the short-term.

"If they don't hike rates, we should see a relief rally in Treasury markets and Brady bonds with spreads tightening but then all eyes will be on the next FOMC meeting in July which will cap the upside," he said.
Opinions were split over whether the Fed would raise U.S. rates or not. In a Reuters survey, a slight majority of U.S. primary dealers believed the Fed would keep key rates unchanged.
The Fed generally announces its decision around 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
Of the most liquid Brady instruments, the Argentine FRBs were unchanged at 92-1/4 bid, while Brazil "C" bonds were down 1/4 at 75-7/8 bid.
Venezuelan DCBs were holding steady at 89-3/4 bid, and FLIRBs unchanged at 90-1/8, while Mexican discounts were slightly off by 1/8 at 91-1/8 bid. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
